hmmt-feb-2005-gen1-04.title: Expand
hmmt-feb-2005-gen1-04.body:
The equation becomes $3x^3+9x^2+15x+9=x^3+9x^2+27x+27$, i.e. $2x^3-12x-18=0$, i.e. $2(x-3)(x^2+3x+3)=0$. The quadratic has discriminant $9-12=-3<0$, so the only real solution is $x=3$ (indeed $27+64+125=216$).

**Answer: $x=3$**

hmmt-feb-2005-gen1-06.title: Sum over the number of votes
hmmt-feb-2005-gen1-06.body:
The probability that exactly $k$ supporters of $A$ vote and exactly $k$ supporters of $B$ vote is $\binom5k^2\cdot\frac1{2^{10}}$. Summing over $k=0,\dots,5$:
$$\frac{1}{1024}\left(1+25+100+100+25+1\right)=\frac{252}{1024}=\frac{63}{256}.$$
(Equivalently $\sum\binom5k^2=\binom{10}5=252$.)

**Answer: $\tfrac{63}{256}$**

hmmt-feb-2005-gen1-10.title: Chinese remainder theorem
hmmt-feb-2005-gen1-10.body:
We need $1000\mid x^2-x=x(x-1)$. Since $x$ and $x-1$ are coprime, $8=2^3$ divides one of them and $125=5^3$ divides one of them. So $x\equiv0$ or $1\pmod{125}$ and $x\equiv0$ or $1\pmod 8$. Running through $x=125,126,250,251,375,376,\dots$ (those $\equiv0,1\pmod{125}$): $125,126,250,251,375$ fail (checking divisibility by $8$ of $x$ or $x-1$), and $376$ works since $376=8\cdot47$ and $375=3\cdot125$. Indeed $376^2=141376$.

**Answer: 376**
